# Plectis Organ Atlas

Do not hand-edit; run: PYTHONPATH=src python3 scripts/build/build_organ_atlas.py --write -->

An **organ** is one accepted public runtime surface: a runnable specimen with a registry row, a claim ceiling, and receipts. This atlas is the comprehension layer over all 88 of them — what each one makes visible, what an agent runs it for, and what it does **not** authorize.

Most organs are **standalone specimens**: they do not call each other. They bind to one shared spine — the architecture kernel (`project -> catalog -> pattern -> standard -> route -> work -> event -> evidence -> explanation -> assimilation`), the evidence-class registry, and the scope limit. A few are **wired** to other named surfaces; each card says which. See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the system shape and [README.md](README.md) for the first run.

> Family labels and counts are navigation metadata: use them to browse and compare source-linked components; maturity, completeness, and launch posture live in separate review records. Evidence classes describe bounded result-record strength for each component. Use this public artifact for local inspection, source records, fixture replay, and component-specific evidence. Operational deployment, external-service use, source-file changes, source mutation, private-root equivalence, proof authority, formal-result authority, and whole-system claims remain separate review topics. Continue from the linked card, paper module, command, or source reference.

## Plectis at a glance — every organ in one line

This is the lowest faithful pass over the public substrate: one row per accepted organ, grouped in canonical family order with Entry & Reveal first. One-lines and scope limits come from `core/paper_module_capsules.json::paper_modules[*].compression`; organ identity and commands come from the accepted registry/atlas model.

### Why the counts are honest

`88` accepted organs · `103` JSON paper-module capsules · `105` Markdown paper modules · `103` JSON paper-module projections. These counts are not expected to match: `15` capsules are mechanism-only, `2` mechanism-only capsules are used by accepted organs through explicit paper-module references, and `15` capsule rows are not accepted-organ atlas rows. Accepted organs, JSON paper-module capsules, and Markdown/JSON paper module projections are distinct surfaces. A count mismatch is expected when capsules describe mechanism-only or ahead-of-registry rows, or when Markdown/JSON projections exist outside the accepted-organ registry.

### First command

Run `plectis tour --card .` for the local first-screen path, then use [AGENT_ROUTES.md](AGENT_ROUTES.md) for task-class routing or the family sections below for per-organ cards.

### Where the public scope stops

Family labels and counts are navigation metadata: use them to browse and compare source-linked components; maturity, completeness, and launch posture live in separate review records. Evidence classes describe bounded result-record strength for each component. Use this public artifact for local inspection, source records, fixture replay, and component-specific evidence. Operational deployment, external-service use, source-file changes, source mutation, private-root equivalence, proof authority, formal-result authority, and whole-system claims remain separate review topics. Continue from the linked card, paper module, command, or source reference.

## How to read a card

Each card carries: **What it makes visible** (plain language) · **For agents** (what to run it for) · **First command** (copyable) · **Scope limit** (where the evidence stops) · **Wiring** (standalone or wired) · **Source relations** (body-free file/shard edge handle) · **Drill down** (paper module, standard, concept/mechanism row, validator command, acceptance receipt).

## Evidence classes

The evidence class tells you how strong a card's backing is. It is a claim-boundary legend, not a score.

| Evidence class | Strength | Counts as substrate progress |
|---|---|---|
| `algorithmic_projection` | 3/5 | yes |
| `bounded_runtime_computation` | 4/5 | yes |
| `external_subprocess_witness` | 4/5 | yes |
| `fixture_echo_smoke` | 1/5 | no (regression/smoke) |
| `fixture_schema_replay` | 2/5 | no (regression/smoke) |
| `semantic_validator` | 5/5 | yes |
| `verified_macro_body_import` | 5/5 | yes |

Where each class stops:

- `algorithmic_projection` — projection mechanics only, not domain-level conclusions
- `bounded_runtime_computation` — bounded in-process runtime computation only, not domain-level conclusions, launch, benchmark, or product authority
- `external_subprocess_witness` — tool witness only, not general proof authority
- `fixture_echo_smoke` — smoke/projection demo only, not behavioral validation, not safety validation, not benchmark claims, and not product progress evidence
- `fixture_schema_replay` — schema/regression fixture only
- `semantic_validator` — validates declared public contract only
- `verified_macro_body_import` — verified non-secret macro body import only, source-linked only, private-system equivalence, launch, or public sharing

## Entry & Reveal

*Microcosm's entry point and what its short guided path actually proves.* (2 organs)

### Cold Reader Route Map

`semantic_validator` · strength 5/5 · Entry & Reveal

- **Organ id:** `cold_reader_route_map`
- **Specialty:** `agent-entry` · `getting-started` · `interesting-parts` · `evaluation` · `provider-ops`
- **Substrate disposition:** `real_substrate_capsule` · real bodies `4` · receipt bodies `0` · fixture role `regression_wrapper_around_real_substrate`
- **What it makes visible:** Matches commands and descriptions to public text and verifies documentation anchors and linked results.
- **First command:** `microcosm cold-reader-route-map run-route-map-bundle --input examples/cold_reader_route_map/exported_cold_reader_route_map_bundle --out receipts/runtime_shell/demo_project/organs/cold_reader_route_map --card`
- **Scope limit:** Matches the introductory commands and descriptions to the public text and resolves their documentation anchors, rejecting an entry with a missing command or receipt reference.
- **Wiring:** wired — consumes the first-screen card as a handoff and sequences/binds named sibling organs (tour, status, authority, workingness, explain, observe, compile) by requiring each route row to point at their commands and receipts. Doctrine-lattice wires_to additions in this row are source-derived from core/mechanism_sources.json upstream_of rows for the organ's hosted mechanism(s); they name structural sibling navigation only, not live run, launch-scope decision, or proof of runtime integration.
- **Source relations:** `140` source-module edges · `4` source files · `16` source shards · `4` target files · `16` target shards · handle `organ-surface-contract::coverage.source_module_file_graph.edges_by_organ[organ_id=cold_reader_route_map]` · drilldown `microcosm organ-topology --organ cold_reader_route_map`
- **Wires to:** `navigation_hologram_route_plane`, `agent_route_observability_runtime`, `pattern_binding_contract`, `doctrine_fact_claim_audit`, `pattern_assimilation_step`, `routing_anti_patterns_registry`, `self_ignorance_coverage_ledger`, `voice_to_doctrine_self_improvement_loop`
- **Drill down:** paper module [`paper_modules/cold_reader_route_map.md`](paper_modules/cold_reader_route_map.md) · standard [`standards/std_microcosm_cold_reader_route_map.json`](standards/std_microcosm_cold_reader_route_map.json) · concept `organ_doctrine_row:cold_reader_route_map.concept_binding` · mechanism `organ_doctrine_row:cold_reader_route_map.mechanism_binding` · validator `python -m microcosm_core.organs.cold_reader_route_map run --input fixtures/first_wave/cold_reader_route_map/input --out receipts/first_wave/cold_reader_route_map` · acceptance `core/acceptance/first_wave_acceptance.json::accepted_current_authority_organs[organ_id=cold_reader_route_map]` · current evidence [`receipts/acceptance/first_wave/cold_reader_route_map_fixture_acceptance.json`](receipts/acceptance/first_wave/cold_reader_route_map_fixture_acceptance.json) · input manifest [`core/fixture_manifests/cold_reader_route_map.fixture_manifest.json`](core/fixture_manifests/cold_reader_route_map.fixture_manifest.json)

### Public Reveal Walkthrough

`bounded_runtime_computation` · strength 4/5 · Entry & Reveal

- **Organ id:** `public_reveal_walkthrough`
- **Specialty:** `getting-started` · `interesting-parts` · `evaluation`
- **Substrate disposition:** `real_substrate_capsule` · real bodies `1` · receipt bodies `0` · fixture role `regression_wrapper_around_real_substrate`
- **What it makes visible:** The walkthrough validator checks audience-specific claim rows and their links to public evidence, including runtime and source references. It produces a board and findings to help a reader follow a claim to supporting material.
- **First command:** `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m microcosm_core.organs.public_reveal_walkthrough run --input fixtures/first_wave/public_reveal_walkthrough/input --out receipts/first_wave/public_reveal_walkthrough`
- **Scope limit:** Follows each audience-specific claim in the walkthrough to its runtime and source evidence, and rejects a claim that has no matching evidence route.
- **Wiring:** wired — validates a reveal path that explicitly names the `microcosm intake` runtime bridge, `formal_math_readiness_extensions`, and the observatory/macro-projection intake board, while itself consuming only fixtures and the shared kernel + evidence/authority spine. Doctrine-lattice wires_to additions in this row are source-derived from core/mechanism_sources.json upstream_of rows for the organ's hosted mechanism(s); they name structural sibling navigation only, not live run, launch-scope decision, or proof of runtime integration.

### Pattern Binding Contract

`semantic_validator` · strength 5/5 · Architecture & Navigation

- **Organ id:** `pattern_binding_contract`
- **Specialty:** `architecture` · `navigation` · `doctrine`
- **Substrate disposition:** `real_substrate_capsule` · real bodies `2` · receipt bodies `0` · fixture role `regression_wrapper_around_real_substrate`
- **What it makes visible:** A pattern binding links a pattern ID to its governing standard, source references and limits. In the fixture, `pb_valid_synthetic_binding` points to `capsule.synthetic_pattern_contract`, a provenance record for the regression harness. The validator checks required fields, reference resolution, duplicate conflicts and private-body markers. It rejects missing references, conflicting duplicate patterns, private source bodies and public claims that exceed their evidence. A separate route-readiness bundle checks whether selector rows resolve through their owning routes.
- **First command:** `microcosm pattern-route-readiness validate-bundle --input examples/pattern_binding_contract/exported_route_readiness_bundle --out /tmp/microcosm-pattern-route-readiness`
- **Scope limit:** Checks each binding's required fields, references and duplicates, and rejects a missing reference, a conflicting duplicate pattern, a private source body or a public claim larger than its evidence.
- **Wiring:** wired — consumes the route-readiness selector contract via pattern_route_readiness (row-to-organ router, route cards, decision matrix, dependency DAG, macro validation report) and imports the real pattern ledger + substrate bindings, atop the shared kernel + evidence/authority spine. Doctrine-lattice wires_to additions in this row are source-derived from core/mechanism_sources.json upstream_of rows for the organ's hosted mechanism(s); they name structural sibling navigation only, not live run, launch-scope decision, or proof of runtime integration.

### Finite Erdos Denominator-Order Certificate Strike

`bounded_runtime_computation` · strength 4/5 · Formal Math & Proof

- **Organ id:** `finite_erdos_denominator_certificate_strike`
- **Specialty:** `formal-math` · `number-theory` · `exact-arithmetic` · `self-falsifying-certificate`
- **Substrate disposition:** `real_substrate_capsule` · real bodies `2` · receipt bodies `0` · fixture role `no_fixture_authority`
- **What it makes visible:** For a finite set of positive integers F and base b ≥ 2, the component computes the exact rational sum S = Σ 1/(bⁿ − 1) = P/Q. It calculates the multiplicative order of b modulo Q, compares it with lcm(F), and independently checks Q using a common denominator. Duplicate support entries are normalized to a set.
- **First command:** `microcosm finite-erdos-denominator-certificate-strike run --input fixtures/first_wave/finite_erdos_denominator_certificate_strike/input --out receipts/first_wave/finite_erdos_denominator_certificate_strike --acceptance-out receipts/acceptance/first_wave/finite_erdos_denominator_certificate_strike_fixture_acceptance.json`
- **Scope limit:** Recomputes the claimed integer fields exactly for one finite set and base, and rejects a forged denominator or order, an empty support, a base below two and the degenerate unit denominator. A pass is an exact computation for that one input.
- **Wiring:** wired — Surfaces microcosm_core.engine_room.finite_denominator_order_certificate as an accepted formal-math organ; it writes public first-wave receipts and does not use external model services, solve Erdos #257, or mutate shared registries at runtime. wires_to names structural sibling navigation only, not live run or proof of runtime integration.
- **Source relations:** `30` source-module edges · `2` source files · `4` source shards · `2` target files · `4` target shards · handle `organ-surface-contract::coverage.source_module_file_graph.edges_by_organ[organ_id=finite_erdos_denominator_certificate_strike]` · drilldown `microcosm organ-topology --organ finite_erdos_denominator_certificate_strike`

### Finance Forecast Evaluation Spine

`external_subprocess_witness` · strength 4/5 · Research & Science Replays

- **Organ id:** `finance_forecast_evaluation_spine`
- **Specialty:** `research-workflows` · `forecasting` · `finance`
- **Substrate disposition:** `real_substrate_capsule` · real bodies `13` · receipt bodies `0` · fixture role `regression_wrapper_around_real_substrate`
- **What it makes visible:** This component reads a matrix of synthetic losses for a baseline and candidate forecasts, paired loss series and a boundary policy. The fixture exercises stationary bootstrap, reality check, superior predictive ability and model confidence set calculations, as well as a Diebold–Mariano comparison. The test fixture has 40 observations. Its reality check, superior predictive ability and model confidence set calls each use 40 bootstrap replicates; a separate stationary-bootstrap index demonstration uses five. The fixture deliberately blocks SciPy imports to exercise a typed refusal of the Harvey–Leybourne–Newbold correction to the paired comparison, regardless of whether SciPy is installed.
- **First command:** `microcosm finance-forecast-evaluation-spine run --input fixtures/first_wave/finance_forecast_evaluation_spine/input --out receipts/first_wave/finance_forecast_evaluation_spine`
- **Scope limit:** Runs the stationary bootstrap, reality check, superior predictive ability, model confidence set and Diebold–Mariano tests on 40 synthetic loss observations, and rejects a lookahead split. The exported bundle reports its declared statistics contract instead of recomputing the tests.
- **Wiring:** standalone_specimen — Extends the finance evaluation bundle with public statistical modules and binds their subprocess witness to strict anti-advice and provenance receipts.

- **What it makes visible:** This fixture exercises copied source for trace parsing, dependency scheduling, source indexing, patch validation, clean-clone isolation, numeric scoring, PageRank and regression-test selection. Its result combines source checks with the outcomes of the individual witnesses. When regression selection would be empty, the example checks the fallback selection. The trace parser also runs its original Node test witness.
- **First command:** `microcosm batch7-macro-engines-capsule run --input fixtures/first_wave/batch7_macro_engines_capsule/input --out receipts/first_wave/batch7_macro_engines_capsule --acceptance-out receipts/acceptance/first_wave/batch7_macro_engines_capsule_fixture_acceptance.json`

### Audio Level RMS Port

`algorithmic_projection` · strength 3/5 · Import, Projection & Drift

- **Organ id:** `batch8_audio_level_rms_port`
- **Specialty:** `source-import` · `provenance` · `drift-control` · `audio`
- **Substrate disposition:** `real_substrate_capsule` · real bodies `1` · receipt bodies `0` · fixture role `regression_wrapper_around_real_substrate`
- **What it makes visible:** `normalized_level` is a Python port of a Swift audio-level calculation. Given float32 samples or int16 samples, it calculates the root mean square, multiplies it by eight and clamps the result to 0–1. Int16 values are divided by 32767. An empty buffer returns zero; an unsupported format raises `ValueError`.
- **First command:** `microcosm batch8-audio-level-rms-port run --input fixtures/first_wave/batch8_audio_level_rms_port/input --out receipts/first_wave/batch8_audio_level_rms_port --acceptance-out receipts/acceptance/first_wave/batch8_audio_level_rms_port_fixture_acceptance.json`
- **Scope limit:** Runs the Python port of the Swift RMS level calculation on the supplied float32 and int16 samples, returning zero for an empty buffer and rejecting an unsupported format with `ValueError`.
- **Wiring:** standalone_specimen — Ports the pure RMS normalization algorithm into public Python and binds it to fixture, receipt, CLI/runtime-shell, standards, and scope limits checks; it does not start macOS audio runtime, capture devices, change source files, publish, or launch.
- **Source relations:** `6` source-module edges · `1` source files · `4` source shards · `1` target files · `4` target shards · handle `organ-surface-contract::coverage.source_module_file_graph.edges_by_organ[organ_id=batch8_audio_level_rms_port]` · drilldown `microcosm organ-topology --organ batch8_audio_level_rms_port`
